newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends stable amid foreign fund moves.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends stable amid foreign fund moves.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed little changed against its U.S. counterpart on Tuesday, with foreign funds flowing into the surging stock market and profits earned in the same market flowing back out, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.522 against Monday's T$27.521 close. Turnover through dealers was an active US$210 million.
Dealers said the local dollar's fall to an intra-day low of T$27.536 in morning trade was due to foreign fund outflows.
"In such a rallying stock market, some cautious foreign funds took profits first and sent them out," said one dealer.
"But in afternoon trade, bullish foreign funds entered to almost balance the trade," the dealer said.

Dealers said foreign equity funds likely would continue to flow into Taiwan to enter the sizzling stock market, which vaulted on Tuesday to a yet another in a series of six-year highs. It has gained 24 percent in 1997 alone.
For Wednesday, dealers expected a similarly stable range of T$27.51-27.54.
